back: Falls in long-run average cost that result from an increase in the scale of output.
The change in output when all inputs are increased in the same proportion in the long run (increasing, constant or decreasing).
The lowest level of output at which long-run average cost is at its minimum.

front: Name six internal economies of scale.
back: Technical, managerial, financial, marketing, purchasing (bulk buying) and risk-bearing.

front: Internal versus external economies of scale?
back: Internal: from the firm's own growth (movement along LRAC). External: from the growth of the industry in an area (shift down of LRAC for all firms).

front: Name three internal diseconomies of scale.
back: Communication problems, coordination and control problems, poor motivation and industrial relations.

front: What does a high minimum efficient scale relative to the market imply?
back: Few firms can reach the lowest cost: a concentrated industry or natural monopoly.

front: If inputs rise 20% and output rises 30%, what are the returns to scale?
back: Increasing returns to scale (output rises by a larger percentage).

front: Why is diminishing returns not the same as decreasing returns to scale?
back: Diminishing returns: one variable factor, others fixed (short run). Decreasing returns to scale: all factors changed together (long run).
